SMTO-UI-0039 — Save your connection changes before showing the raw value

GUID: 6697b4ce-0857-4e58-8ec4-860387cb1244
Slug: ui-http-unsaved-changes
Domain: UI · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • You changed this connection's settings but haven't saved them yet. SMTO won't open the raw saved value now, because your unsaved changes would be lost or mixed up. Nothing was saved or changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Select Save at the top of the parameter to keep the changes you made to the connection. Once your changes are saved, the raw value you open will include them.
  2. If you don't want those changes, choose another parameter in the list (or reload the page) and confirm that you want to discard them, then open this parameter again. This clears your unsaved edits so the raw value can be opened safely.
  3. Open Advanced: reveal and replace raw saved value and select Reveal & edit value. With no unsaved connection changes, SMTO can show the raw value.

What success looks like

  • The raw saved value appears in the value box, and the page says "Value revealed".

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste the connection's password or key into what you send.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Reveal was requested for an HTTP connection parameter while its connection-profile editor has unsaved changes, so the raw stored value was not fetched.

What this means

  • Reveal is requested while the HTTP public configuration editor still has unsaved changes. The shown control rejects this local action before its dependent submission. Earlier requests and saved state are unaffected by this validation result; server-side authority remains authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • Reveal is requested while the HTTP public configuration editor still has unsaved changes.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the pending public edits and the current saved revision.

How to fix it

  • parameter_editor.js revealParameterValue() presents ui_http_unsaved_changes when state.httpEditor.isDirty() is true, before POST the parameter reveal endpoint (POST /api/agent/parameters/:key/reveal). Save the public profile changes (PATCH with public_http_profile) or discard them, then reveal the raw value.
  • Save the intended public configuration changes before revealing the current raw saved parameter value.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Intended public changes are saved before the exact current raw parameter is revealed.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The shown control rejects this local action before its dependent submission. Earlier requests and saved state are unaffected by this validation result; server-side authority remains authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
